overview: This 329-page file traces debates over Japanese labor policy during the U.S. Occupation in 1948–49, especially bargaining and strike rights for government workers. Diplomatic memoranda, SCAP reports, union agreements, wage tables, court records, and Soviet commentary document economic hardship and competing approaches to labor reform.
interest: It places U.S.–SCAP policy disputes alongside Japanese contracts, wage data, union petitions, and bilingual Supreme Court records.
